error_note: A 7.5 h value after an unspecified (XXX) challenge is not a baseline glucose, so 'low' has no defined meaning as hypoglycemia. Obligate hypoglycemia in a familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy subtype also looks doubtful and hypoglycemia is shared by 207 diseases.
Hypertyrosinemia in BCS1L-related complex III deficiency is secondary to hepatic dysfunction, not a characteristic or diagnostic finding.
Neutropenia does occur in APL as part of pancytopenia, but it is shared by a very large number of marrow and other disorders and does not point to APL.
A 45 min value after an unspecified challenge is not a baseline glucose, so low is not defined as hypoglycemia; hypoglycemia is also only occasional in this disease and highly nonspecific.

A pleural fluid nucleated cell count is not a measure of pleural morphology, and a low count has no pathological reading. The count has no recognised bearing on congenital pulmonary airway malformation.

This is a lactose tolerance test timepoint, where a glucose rise is the normal response and the test is read for lactase deficiency; high here needs its own criteria and is not how hyperglycemia of neonatal diabetes is shown.
A low 30 min glucose after oral lactose means a flat curve (lactose malabsorption), not hypoglycemia. Hypoglycemia is also only an occasional, nonspecific feature of this disorder.

The high direction is sound (homocysteine is mildly raised in AHCY deficiency), but the low direction arises only from the nondirectional parent term 'Abnormal circulating homocysteine concentration' and low homocysteine is not a feature.
C-peptide rises physiologically 1 h after glucose, so high on this timed code needs challenge-specific criteria; the disease phenotype is C-peptide inappropriately high during hypoglycemia.
Raised ACTH is characteristic of triple-A syndrome, but this is a post-glucose timepoint code rather than the baseline morning ACTH on which that finding is established.
The disease record lists AChR antibody positivity as excluded (0%); congenital myasthenic syndromes are by definition seronegative, so a positive association is the reverse of the truth.
A negative IgE to one grass cannot rule out raised IgE to plant products in general; the term is far broader than the single allergen tested.

Colchicine poisoning causes lactic acidosis, so the relevant direction is high; low lactate has no pathological meaning and was reached through the near-root term 'Abnormality of acid-base homeostasis'. The code is also an unspecified-challenge timepoint.
Raised hematocrit is the defining finding of Chuvash polycythemia, but this code is fetal blood, which has its own reference ranges and is not the specimen in which the disease is recognised.
ACTH deficiency is only an occasional component of these combined pituitary hormone deficiencies, and the challenge is unspecified, so what counts as a low stimulated ACTH is undefined.
The disease record says abnormal CSF is explicitly NOT a feature of SPG12. A low CSF lymphocyte fraction is in any case neither a CSF morphology finding nor pathological.
A low barley pollen-specific IgE is a normal result and says nothing about total immunoglobulin concentrations, which is what the bridging phenotype in lysinuric protein intolerance refers to.
The disease record lists antinuclear antibody positivity as excluded (0%), so the positive association is unsupported.
The disease record lists increased lactate as excluded (0%) in this disorder; the positive association contradicts it.
Antiphospholipid antibodies are a very rare (<5%) feature of autoimmune polyendocrinopathy type 3, and the code is a panel with no single high result.

Lactate 4 h after an unspecified challenge (possibly exercise, glucose or ischemic testing) cannot be read against a resting reference interval, so high does not by itself establish increased circulating lactate.
The mix is beef, chicken, egg yolk, pork and turkey: all animal foods. The plant-based food allergen term is the wrong one.
A single-frequency, single-ear threshold is one narrow component of audiometry, and audiometry documents the hearing loss component rather than diagnosing Waardenburg syndrome.
A low allergen-specific IgE is the normal, non-sensitised state and is not an abnormal circulating immunoglobulin concentration, which refers to total immunoglobulin classes.
Audiometry characterises the hearing loss but, as the curator text itself says, cannot identify this genetic subtype; it is a phenotyping test common to every hearing-loss disorder.
The breath hydrogen test is appropriate only with a sucrose challenge; this code leaves the challenge unspecified (XXX), so an increase could equally reflect lactose, fructose or lactulose testing.

The band shown is G1 (eGFR >= 90), a normal or high GFR. It indicates chronic kidney disease only with separate evidence of kidney damage persisting over 3 months, so the GFR result itself does not indicate the phenotype.
Triglyceride >= 1000 mg/dL is a risk factor for acute pancreatitis, not evidence that the patient has it; the curator text says so but the relation is coded as INDICATES.
A raised TSH alone cannot separate compensated (subclinical) from overt hypothyroidism; that needs a normal free T4, which this code does not carry.

NYHA class grades functional limitation in a patient already known to have cardiac disease; it is a severity classification, not evidence that establishes heart failure, and it says nothing about congestion.
NYHA class II-IV grades symptoms in a patient already diagnosed with heart disease; it stages severity and does not by itself indicate the diagnosis of heart failure.
